decisions.reason: Its fit with the firm's core authentication and secure-communication platform supports retention, but two years without visible market evidence suggest results may be drifting below aspiration.
As a close but feature-like extension, it is more likely to be withdrawn if standalone demand has remained below aspiration and the capability can be folded into broader signing solutions.
Because it rests directly on the firm's core security architecture know-how and remains reusable across offerings, management would still keep it unless a clear sustained shortfall is evident.
This more niche product is the strongest candidate for problemistic search and resource reallocation after several years without visible traction relative to aspiration levels.

Compliance-focused security still fits the firm's regulated customer base and capabilities, so boundedly rational management would usually retain it, though recent weak visibility raises the risk of exit.
